definitionEn: not suitable or acceptable for a particular situation or occasion
situation: Criticising behaviour, clothes, jokes or comments that do not fit the rules or expectations of a particular situation.

examples.text: Posting photos of patients online is [[inappropriate]] for a nurse, even if their faces are hidden.
Some parents think the film is [[inappropriate]] for children under twelve because of its violence.
The comedian apologised for making an [[inappropriate]] joke about the victims of the flood.

texts: It would be [[inappropriate]] for me to comment on the case.
Flip-flops are [[inappropriate]] footwear for a mountain hike.
The teacher was fired for sending [[inappropriate]] messages to students.

badCollocation.noteRu: Если одежда не подошла по размеру, говорят the wrong size. Inappropriate — «неуместный» с точки зрения норм и приличий.

collocationTask.prompt: It would be ___ for me to comment on an ongoing investigation.
collocationTask.explanationRu: It would be inappropriate for me to comment — вежливое «мне не подобает комментировать». Inadequate — «недостаточный», unsuitable — «неподходящий по свойствам», incorrect — «неверный».

nuance.text: Checking your phone during a minute's silence is deeply [[inappropriate]].
nuance.explanationRu: Inappropriate — неуместный с точки зрения норм и приличий. Unsuitable — неподходящий по практическим качествам (обувь, квартира, кандидат); о поведении так не говорят, и deeply unsuitable звучит странно.

fixIt.text: His [[inadequate]] behaviour at the office party got him into trouble with HR.
fixIt.explanationRu: Inadequate — «недостаточный», а не русское «неадекватный». Неуместное, неприличное поведение — inappropriate behaviour.

reply.context: Your friend asks: "Is it OK to wear jeans to my cousin's wedding? The invitation says 'black tie'."
options: Sure, jeans are totally inappropriate, so go for it!
Jeans are deemed inappropriate attire pursuant to the stated dress code.
I'd say jeans would be pretty inappropriate if it's black tie.
reply.explanationRu: Inappropriate — «неуместный»: джинсы на свадьбе с дресс-кодом black tie. В первом ответе inappropriate ошибочно звучит как одобрение, а второй слишком официален для разговора с другом.

definitionEn: how often something, especially a disease or crime, happens in a group or area
senseNote: Не путайте с incident — «происшествие». Incidence — частота, с которой что-то случается.
situation: Reporting how common a disease, crime or problem is among a particular group of people or in a place.

examples.text: There is a high [[incidence]] of asthma among children living near busy roads.
Since the new street lights were installed, the [[incidence]] of burglary in the area has fallen sharply.
The study found a lower [[incidence]] of heart disease among people who ate fish twice a week.

texts: Doctors are alarmed by the rising [[incidence]] of diabetes in teenagers.
The [[incidence]] of road accidents drops sharply in summer.
Coastal towns report a higher [[incidence]] of skin cancer.

badCollocation.noteRu: С incidence говорят high или low, а не big и small: a high incidence of crime.

collocationTask.explanationRu: A high incidence of — «высокая частота (заболевания)». Incident — отдельное происшествие, а quantity и amount о болезнях так не употребляют.

nuance.text: Researchers have recorded a sharp rise in the [[incidence]] of food allergies.
nuance.explanationRu: Incidence — частота, с которой что-то случается (болезни, преступления). Incident — одно конкретное происшествие, и «рост происшествия аллергии» — бессмыслица.

reverse.text: Police are investigating an [[incident]] outside the stadium last night.
reverse.explanationRu: Отдельное событие, происшествие — an incident. Incidence — статистическая частота, её нельзя «расследовать».

fixIt.text: The [[spread]] of diabetes is much higher in cities than in rural areas.
fixIt.explanationRu: Spread — процесс распространения, он не бывает «выше». Чтобы сравнить, как часто встречается болезнь, говорят incidence (или prevalence).

rewrite.original: Lung cancer is much more common among smokers.
rewrite.frame: There is a much higher ____ lung cancer among smokers.
rewrite.explanationRu: A higher incidence of — «более высокая частота случаев».

definitionEn: wanting to do something, or leaning towards a particular opinion
senseNote: Здесь — «склонный, расположенный что-то сделать или думать»: I'm inclined to agree. Не «наклонный» и не «с задатками» (musically inclined).
situation: Saying that you feel like doing something, or that you tend to believe one opinion more than another.

examples.text: Having heard both sides, I'm [[inclined]] to agree with Maria, although I'd like to see the figures first.
It was such a lovely evening that nobody felt [[inclined]] to go home early.
If you're so [[inclined]], the museum also offers late-night tours on Fridays.

texts: I'm [[inclined]] to believe her story, strange as it sounds.
The committee seems [[inclined]] to accept the proposal.
Few people are [[inclined]] to argue with a hungry toddler.

badCollocation.noteRu: После inclined ставят инфинитив: inclined to talk. Inclined for + -ing не говорят; о настроении — in the mood for talking.

collocationTask.prompt: I'm ___ to agree with you on this point.
collocationTask.explanationRu: I'm inclined to agree — вежливое «склонен согласиться». Liable to — о вероятности неприятного, с leaning нужно towards, а после capable — of + -ing.

nuance.text: I'm [[inclined]] to think the second candidate is stronger, but I haven't decided yet.
nuance.explanationRu: Inclined to think — «склоняюсь к мнению», осторожная оценка. Willing — «готов сделать что-то, если попросят»; willing to think звучит так, будто вас уговаривают подумать.

reverse.text: Are you [[willing]] to work weekends if necessary?
reverse.explanationRu: На собеседовании спрашивают о готовности выполнить требование — willing. Inclined выражает внутреннее желание или мнение, а не согласие.

fixIt.text: Having read the report, I'm [[prone]] to agree with the critics, but I'd like to hear your view.
fixIt.explanationRu: Prone to — склонность к чему-то плохому (prone to accidents, prone to colds). Осторожно выразить мнение — I'm inclined to agree.

wordFormation.text: I have no [[inclination]] to move back to my home town.

reply.context: In a meeting, your manager asks: "Should we hire the candidate with more experience or the one with better ideas?"
options: I'm inclined to go with the one with better ideas, but it's a close call.
I'm inclined to hire them both, because the law says we must.
Yeah, whatever, I'm inclined or something, dunno.
reply.explanationRu: I'm inclined to — «склоняюсь к…», осторожное мнение. Inclined не значит «обязан» (это required или obliged), а третий ответ слишком небрежен для рабочей встречи.

rewrite.original: I tend to agree with you, although I'm not completely sure.
rewrite.frame: I'm ____ agree with you, although I'm not completely sure.

definitionEn: the act of adding someone or something to a group, list or collection
senseNote: Здесь — «включение в состав, список, книгу». В значении «инклюзия» (равные возможности для всех) слово тоже встречается: social inclusion.
situation: Talking about someone or something being added to a team, list, report or collection, often as a surprise or a decision.

examples.text: Fans were delighted by the [[inclusion]] of two local teenagers in the national squad.
The [[inclusion]] of older patients in the trial made the results more reliable.
The dictionary's [[inclusion]] of slang words like 'selfie' annoyed some traditional readers.

texts: Her [[inclusion]] on the shortlist came as a complete surprise.
The editor questioned the [[inclusion]] of so many photographs.
The coach defended his [[inclusion]] of an untested young goalkeeper.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Включение света или прибора» — switching on (turning on) the light. Inclusion — включение в состав, список или группу.

collocationTask.prompt: Her ___ in the Olympic team was announced yesterday.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Включение человека в команду или список — inclusion. Insertion — вставка предмета, enclosure — вложение (в письмо), incorporation — объединение, слияние.

nuance.text: The [[inclusion]] of her poem in the school textbook made her briefly famous.
nuance.explanationRu: Inclusion — включение в состав, в список, в книгу. Involvement — участие, причастность; стихотворение не может «участвовать» в учебнике.

reverse.text: Police are investigating his [[involvement]] in the robbery.
reverse.explanationRu: Причастность к преступлению — involvement in. Inclusion — когда кого-то включают в список или команду, а не участие в событии.

fixIt.text: The [[including]] of breakfast in the price makes this hotel excellent value.
fixIt.explanationRu: Перед of нужно существительное: the inclusion of breakfast. Форма the including of — ошибка.

wordFormation.text: The [[inclusion]] of a map at the start of the novel helps readers follow the journey.

reply.context: A friend who follows football texts: "Did you see who's in the squad for the World Cup?"
options: Affirmative; the squad inclusions have been duly noted.
Yes! The goalkeeper's inclusion is a huge surprise; he's only eighteen.
Yes, but the inclusion of my TV failed, so I missed the announcement.
reply.explanationRu: The goalkeeper's inclusion — «то, что вратаря включили в состав». В третьем ответе inclusion ошибочно значит «включение телевизора» (это switching on), а первый звучит как официальный протокол.

definitionEn: welcoming and treating fairly people of all backgrounds, abilities and identities
senseNote: Здесь — «открытый для всех, никого не исключающий». О цене inclusive значит «включая всё»: inclusive of VAT, all-inclusive.
situation: Describing a place, group or policy that makes sure nobody is left out because of who they are.

examples.text: The school prides itself on being [[inclusive]], with lifts, sign-language classes and support for every learner.
The company rewrote its job adverts in more [[inclusive]] language to attract a wider range of applicants.
Our running club is fully [[inclusive]]: beginners, older runners and wheelchair users all train together.

texts: The festival aims to be [[inclusive]] and affordable for families.
Good design should be [[inclusive]], not an afterthought for disabled users.
The new textbook uses more [[inclusive]] examples from different cultures.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Инклюзивный ребёнок» — калька. По-английски: a child with special educational needs. Inclusive описывает школу, класс или политику, а не самого ребёнка.

collocationTask.prompt: ___ language avoids words that might exclude or offend people.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Inclusive language — язык, который никого не исключает и не задевает. Comprehensive — «всеобъемлющий», collective — «коллективный», integral — «неотъемлемый».

nuance.text: The new playground is fully [[inclusive]], with swings that wheelchair users can enjoy too.
nuance.explanationRu: Inclusive — устроенный так, чтобы участвовать могли все (о месте, дизайне, политике). Tolerant — терпимый, это черта человека; площадка не может быть «терпимой».

reverse.text: My grandparents are surprisingly [[tolerant]] of my loud music.
reverse.explanationRu: Терпимо относиться к чему-то — be tolerant of. Inclusive описывает, открыто ли место или сообщество для всех, а не терпение к шуму.

fixIt.text: Our office is now fully [[included]], with ramps and quiet rooms for staff who need them.
fixIt.explanationRu: Included — «включённый» (в список, в цену). О месте, которое открыто и удобно для всех, говорят inclusive.

wordFormation.text: Teachers are trained to make their lessons more [[inclusive]] for children with dyslexia.

reply.context: Your colleague asks: "How can we make the office party better for everyone this year?"
options: Let's make it more inclusive: only managers should come this time.
Inclusivity parameters shall be operationalised forthwith.
Let's make it more inclusive. Not everyone drinks, so we need proper alcohol-free options.
reply.explanationRu: Inclusive — такой, чтобы всем было комфортно, в том числе тем, кто не пьёт. «Только для менеджеров» — наоборот, исключает людей, а второй ответ звучит как канцелярский жаргон.

definitionEn: to have to pay or suffer something unpleasant because of your own actions
situation: Explaining that costs, debts, fines or someone's anger result from a decision you made or something you did.

examples.text: The airline [[incurred]] huge losses when it had to ground its entire fleet for a month.
You will [[incur]] a fee of £50 if you change your flight less than a day before departure.
By criticising the chef in front of the guests, she [[incurred]] his lasting anger.

texts: Late payments may [[incur]] an extra charge of ten per cent.
Try not to [[incur]] the wrath of the head chef.
Students often [[incur]] large debts during their studies.

badCollocation.noteRu: Incur — только о неприятном: расходах, долгах, штрафах. Прибыль получают: make a profit.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Incur — нести что-то неприятное: incur losses («нести убытки»). Прибыль и доходы (profits, gains, savings) не incur, а make или earn.

nuance.text: The company [[incurred]] heavy losses after the factory fire.
nuance.explanationRu: Incur — понести расходы или убытки самому. Caused heavy losses значило бы, что компания нанесла убытки кому-то другому, а смысл здесь противоположный.

reverse.text: The storm [[caused]] serious damage to the harbour.
reverse.explanationRu: Шторм сам ничего не «несёт» и не платит, он причиняет ущерб: caused damage. Incur говорят о том, кто несёт расходы.

fixIt.text: Passengers who change their booking online will [[receive]] a small administration fee.
fixIt.explanationRu: Receive a fee — «получить деньги», то есть наоборот. Если придётся заплатить сбор, говорят incur a fee.

reply.context: Your manager emails: "Can we move the conference from February to March?"
options: Sure, and we'd incur a nice discount from the hotel too!
We can, but we'd incur a cancellation fee of about £2,000 from the hotel.
Nah, fees and stuff, dunno, kinda pricey.
reply.explanationRu: Incur a fee — «понести расходы, заплатить сбор». Скидку не incur — её get или receive, а третий ответ слишком небрежен для письма начальнику.

rewrite.original: If you pay late, you will have to pay an extra charge.
rewrite.frame: Late payment will ____ an extra charge.
rewrite.explanationRu: Incur a charge — «повлечь за собой дополнительный сбор».

definitionEn: a sign or measurement that shows the state of something or how it is changing
senseNote: Здесь — «показатель, признак». В британской машине indicator — ещё и «поворотник».
situation: Talking about a figure or sign, such as unemployment or blood pressure, that helps you judge a situation.

examples.text: Unemployment is one of the most important [[indicators]] of how healthy an economy is.
Blood pressure is a useful [[indicator]] of your general heart health.
Attendance is not always a reliable [[indicator]] of how much students are actually learning.

texts: Rising house prices are often seen as a reliable [[indicator]] of confidence.
A child's vocabulary is a good [[indicator]] of how much they read.
Falling sales can be an early [[indicator]] of trouble.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Высокие показатели продаж» — strong sales figures. Indicator — признак или измеритель, а не результат, который бывает «высоким».

collocationTask.explanationRu: Economic indicator — «экономический показатель», устойчивое сочетание. Indication — намёк, признак того, что что-то вероятно; sign и symptom с economic так не употребляют.

nuance.text: Inflation and unemployment are the two [[indicators]] that investors watch most closely.
nuance.explanationRu: Indicator — измеримый показатель, за которым следят (инфляция, безработица). Indication — намёк или признак того, что что-то вероятно; за «намёками» так не следят.

reverse.text: There is every [[indication]] that the talks will succeed.
reverse.explanationRu: There is every indication that — «всё говорит о том, что». Это устойчивое выражение, indicator сюда не подходит.

fixIt.text: Life expectancy is a key [[exponent]] of a nation's health.
fixIt.explanationRu: Exponent — «показатель степени» в математике или «сторонник идеи». Показатель, по которому судят о ситуации, — indicator.

wordFormation.text: Test scores are only one [[indicator]] of a school's success.

rewrite.original: The number of job adverts shows quite reliably how the economy is doing.
rewrite.frame: The number of job adverts is a reliable ____ how the economy is doing.

definitionEn: something that shows clearly how bad or unfair a system or situation is
senseNote: Здесь — переносное «убийственное свидетельство провала»: a damning indictment of the system. Юридическое «обвинительный акт» (в основном в США) встречается реже.
situation: Commenting that a situation, report or fact clearly shows the failure of an institution, system or society.

examples.text: The number of children living in poverty is a damning [[indictment]] of the city's housing policy.
The fact that nurses need food banks is a shocking [[indictment]] of how we value care work.
The documentary is a powerful [[indictment]] of the way the fashion industry exploits factory workers.

texts: The report is a damning [[indictment]] of the prison system.
Such long waiting lists are a sad [[indictment]] of the health service.
The novel is a bitter [[indictment]] of small-town gossip and hypocrisy.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Тяжёлое обвинение» в этом смысле — a damning или scathing indictment. Heavy с indictment не сочетается.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Damning indictment — «убийственное свидетельство провала». Heavy, hard и rough с indictment не сочетаются: это кальки с «тяжёлый, жёсткий».

nuance.text: It is a sad [[indictment]] of modern society that so many old people feel lonely.
nuance.explanationRu: Indictment — факт, который сам по себе обличает систему: «печальное свидетельство». Criticism — чья-то критика, высказанное мнение; a sad criticism of society that… так не говорят.

reverse.text: Thank you for the constructive [[criticism]]: it really helped me improve the essay.
reverse.explanationRu: Конструктивная критика — constructive criticism. Indictment — суровое обличение, оно не бывает «конструктивным».

fixIt.text: The film is a damning [[accusation]] of the way big cities treat homeless people.
fixIt.explanationRu: Accusation of — обвинение человека в конкретном проступке (accusation of theft). Обличение системы или общества — an indictment of.

reply.context: In a debate, someone says: "Our city has three new luxury hotels but no public swimming pool."
options: Exactly, and I'd say that's a sad indictment of the council's priorities.
Yes, what a wonderful indictment of the council's generosity!
lol yeah, total indictment vibes, whatever.
reply.explanationRu: A sad indictment of — «печальное свидетельство» провала или неправильных приоритетов. Indictment не бывает похвалой, а третий ответ слишком небрежен для дебатов.

definitionEn: belonging to a place naturally, rather than coming from somewhere else
situation: Describing peoples, languages, plants or animals that have always lived in a region, not arrived from elsewhere.

examples.text: Gardeners are encouraged to plant [[indigenous]] trees, which support more local wildlife than imported species.
The university offers courses in several [[indigenous]] languages of South America.
The dam was stopped after [[indigenous]] communities proved the land had belonged to them for centuries.

texts: Koalas are [[indigenous]] to the forests of eastern Australia.
The museum displays [[indigenous]] art from across the Pacific.
Many [[indigenous]] languages have fewer than a thousand speakers.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Коренной москвич» — a native Muscovite или born and bred in Moscow. Indigenous говорят о коренных народах, растениях и животных, а не о горожанах.

collocationTask.prompt: The kiwi is ___ to New Zealand.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Indigenous to (или native to) — «исконно обитает в». Local, original и domestic с to в этом значении не употребляют.

nuance.text: Potatoes are [[indigenous]] to South America and only reached Europe in the sixteenth century.
nuance.explanationRu: Indigenous — исконно происходящий из этого места (о видах, народах). Local — просто местный, из ближайшей округи; local to South America о растениях не говорят.

reverse.text: We bought fresh cheese and bread at the [[local]] market.
reverse.explanationRu: Рынок рядом с домом — local market. Indigenous говорят о народах, языках, растениях и животных, а не о магазинах и рынках.

fixIt.text: The island is home to more than forty [[original]] species of bird that live nowhere else.
fixIt.explanationRu: Original — «первоначальный, оригинальный». Виды, которые исконно обитают на острове, — indigenous (или native) species.

rewrite.original: This plant grows naturally only in the mountains of Chile.
rewrite.frame: This plant is ____ the mountains of Chile.

definitionEn: the qualities that make a person or thing different from all others
senseNote: Individuality — качество, а не человек: «он яркая индивидуальность» — he has a strong personality.
situation: Talking about the special character, style or way of thinking that makes someone clearly different from other people.

examples.text: Strict uniform rules leave pupils very little room to express their [[individuality]].
Critics admire the [[individuality]] of her paintings: you can recognise one from across the room.
A good manager encourages teamwork without crushing each employee's [[individuality]].

texts: Every child's [[individuality]] should be respected in the classroom.
The old town has lost much of its [[individuality]] to chain stores.
Her singing voice has real [[individuality]] and warmth.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Яркая индивидуальность» (о человеке) — a strong personality. Individuality — качество, а не человек, и с bright не сочетается.

collocationTask.prompt: Teenagers often use fashion to express their ___.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Express your individuality — «выражать свою индивидуальность». Singularity — термин науки, identification — опознание или удостоверение, particularity — редкое книжное слово.

nuance.text: Each hand-made cup has its own [[individuality]], so no two are exactly alike.
nuance.explanationRu: Individuality — неповторимость конкретного человека или вещи. Individualism — идеология, убеждение, что личная независимость важнее общих интересов; у чашки её быть не может.

fixIt.text: The designer wanted every room of the hotel to have its own [[individual]] style and feel.
fixIt.explanationRu: Individual — «отдельный человек» или «отдельный». Своеобразие, неповторимость — individuality.

wordFormation.text: Mass production leaves little room for [[individuality]] in furniture design.

reply.context: Your friend says: "I'm thinking of dyeing my hair bright blue. Is that too much?"
options: Go for it! It'll really show off your individuality.
Go for it! Individuality means looking exactly like everybody else.
Your proposal to alter your hair colour is approved in the interests of individuality.
reply.explanationRu: Show off your individuality — «подчеркнуть свою индивидуальность». Индивидуальность — как раз непохожесть на других, а третий ответ звучит как официальное разрешение, а не совет другу.
